'''Dorian Schuyler Abbot''' is an American [[geophysicist]]. He is a professor at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Powell |first1=Michael |title=M.I.T.’s Choice of Lecturer Ignited Criticism. So Did Its Decision to Cancel. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/20/us/dorian-abbot-mit.html |website=The New York Times |date=20 October 2021}}</ref>

== Education ==
Abbot was educated at [[Harvard University]], where he earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in 2004 in physics, then received a [[Master of Science]] (2004) and [[Ph.D.]] (2008) in applied mathematics from the [[Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences]]. His dissertation was titled ''A high-latitude convective cloud feedback''.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=A high-latitude convective cloud feedback|date=2008|language=English|first=Dorian Schuyler|last=Abbot|degree=Ph.D.|publisher=Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences|oclc=934916756}}</ref> Abbot's doctoral advisor was {{Interlanguage link|Eli Tziperman|qid=Q58065299}}. From 2008 to 2009, he was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] in the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences at Harvard University. Abbot conducted post doctoral research in geophysical sciences from 2009 to 2011 at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Abbot|first=Dorian|title=Curriculum Vitae|url=https://d3qi0qp55mx5f5.cloudfront.net/geosci/i/basic_pages/AbbotCV2021.pdf?mtime=1619727403|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-20|website=University of Chicago|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211016011345/https://d3qi0qp55mx5f5.cloudfront.net/geosci/i/basic_pages/AbbotCV2021.pdf?mtime=1619727403 |archive-date=16 October 2021 }}</ref>

== Career ==
Abbot became an assistant professor of geophysical sciences at University of Chicago in 2011. He became an associate professor in 2015 and a full professor in 2024. Abbot uses low-order mathematical models and [[numerical models]] to research climates, [[paleoclimate]]s, [[planetary habitability]], and [[exoplanet]]s.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Dorian Abbot|work=People|publisher=University of Chicago Geophysical Sciences|url=https://geosci.uchicago.edu/people/dorian-abbot/|access-date=2021-10-20}}</ref>

=== MIT lecture cancellation ===
In 2020, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology invited Abbot to discuss his work on extraterrestrial life in the public Carlson Lecture. The [[COVID-19 pandemic]] postponed the lecture to the following year. In September 2021, the host department cancelled Abbot's public lecture and offered Abbot a future private lecture to its faculty and students.<ref name="PowellNYT">{{Cite web |last=Powell |first=Michael |date=October 20, 2021 |title=M.I.T.'s Choice of Lecturer Ignited Criticism. So Did Its Decision to Cancel. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/20/us/dorian-abbot-mit.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020171033/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/20/us/dorian-abbot-mit.html |archive-date=20 October 2021 |access-date=2021-10-25 |website=The New York Times |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Flaherty2021">{{Cite web|last=Flaherty|first=Colleen|date=October 19, 2021|title=MIT deals with fallout from canceled lecture|url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2021/10/19/mit-deals-fallout-canceled-lecture|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Inside Higher Ed|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019083645/https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2021/10/19/mit-deals-fallout-canceled-lecture |archive-date=19 October 2021 }}</ref> According to the department, the cancellation responded to objections from faculty and students to a ''[[Newsweek]]'' editorial co-written by Abbot in the prior month.<ref name="PowellNYT"/><ref name="Carden2021">{{cite news |last=Carden |first=Kaylee |title=EAPS department annual Carlson Lecture canceled over speaker Dorian Abbot’s comments on DEI |date=14 October 2021 |url=https://thetech.com/2021/10/14/carlson-lecture-cancellation |access-date=10 October 2025}}</ref><ref name="Flaherty2021"/><ref name="Sobey2021">{{Cite news|last=Sobey|first=Rick|date=October 5, 2021|title=MIT cancels professor lecture after backlash against him, university cites 'distractions'|url=https://www.bostonherald.com/2021/10/05/mit-cancels-professor-lecture-after-backlash-against-him-university-cites-distractions/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Boston Herald|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211006014316/https://www.bostonherald.com/2021/10/05/mit-cancels-professor-lecture-after-backlash-against-him-university-cites-distractions/ |archive-date=6 October 2021 }}</ref> 

In the editorial, Abbot and Stanford professor Ivan Marinovic argued for renewed focus on individual talent in university admissions and hiring.<ref name="PowellNYT"/> They called for abolishing "group membership" preferences, including [[Affirmative action in the United States|race]] and [[legacy preference]] in university admissions, and criticized aspects of university [[Diversity, equity, and inclusion|diversity policy]]. They recalled how the racial ideology of [[Nazi Germany]] "drove many of the best scholars out" of the universities, and called this "a warning of the consequences of viewing group membership as more important than merit."<ref name="Carden2021"/><ref name="Abbot Marinovic 2021">{{cite web | last1=Abbot | first1=Dorian S. | last2=Marinovic | first2=Ivan | title=The diversity problem on campus - Opinion | website=Newsweek | date=12 August 2021 | url=https://www.newsweek.com/diversity-problem-campus-opinion-1618419 | access-date=2021-10-29}}</ref>

Defending the lecture cancellation, senior MIT officials stated that controversy over Abbott's views on diversity would "overshadow" the scientific content of his public lecture.<ref name="PowellNYT"/><ref>{{Cite web|last=Schmidt |first=Martin|date=October 7, 2021|title=Letter to the community from MIT provost|url=https://orgchart.mit.edu/node/6/letters_to_community/important-update-re-eaps|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-24|website=MIT|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011202722/https://orgchart.mit.edu/node/6/letters_to_community/important-update-re-eaps |archive-date=11 October 2021 }}</ref> Abbot ultimately delivered his lecture on planetary science to a larger audience hosted by the [[James Madison Program in American Ideals and Institutions]] at [[Princeton University]] on the same day as the cancelled event.<ref name="Flaherty2021"/><ref name="Mayberry2021">{{Cite web|last=Mayberry|first=Carly|date=October 12, 2021|title=Geophysicist 'Canceled' by MIT Honored With Award While Thousands Register for His Lecture|url=https://www.newsweek.com/geophysicist-canceled-mit-honored-award-while-thousands-register-his-lecture-1637820|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-28|website=Newsweek|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211012173545/https://www.newsweek.com/geophysicist-canceled-mit-honored-award-while-thousands-register-his-lecture-1637820 |archive-date=12 October 2021 }}</ref> Abbot was a guest on [[Tucker Carlson Today|''Tucker Carlson Tonight'']]<ref>{{Cite web|last=Creitz|first=Charles|date=October 20, 2021|title= Professor Dorian Abbot: I was canceled for basing admissions on merit|url=https://www.foxnews.com/media/professor-dorian-abbot-i-was-canceled-merit|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-28|website=Fox News|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021025232/https://www.foxnews.com/media/professor-dorian-abbot-i-was-canceled-merit |archive-date=21 October 2021 }}</ref> and [[CNN]]<ref name="CNN 2021">{{cite web | title=Politics overshadowing scientific work | website=CNN | date=2021-10-23 | url=https://www.cnn.com/videos/tv/2021/10/23/geophysicist-canceled-at-mit-over-personal-politics.cnn | access-date=2021-10-29}}</ref> to discuss the cancellation. He also received a Hero of Intellectual Freedom Award from the [[American Council of Trustees and Alumni]].<ref name="Mayberry2021"/>

Following public outrage and rebukes from MIT faculty about free expression, the university held forums at which attending faculty were polled on free speech questions.<ref name="Flaherty2021"/><ref name="PowellNYT"/> 60% of attendees felt that their voices were "constrained" at MIT; a new MIT Free Speech Alliance cited these findings as a call to action.<ref name="MFSA 2021">{{cite web | url=https://www.mitfreespeech.org/ | title=MIT Free Speech Alliance (MFSA) | author=<!--Not stated--> | website=MIT Free Speech Alliance | access-date=May 6, 2023 | quote=The barrage of negative press and public outrage resulting from MIT cancelling Dr. Abbot ... | archive-date=2021-11-06  | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211106205018/https://www.mitfreespeech.org/ | url-status=deviated }}</ref>{{Independent source inline|date=October 2025}} In December 2022, responding to the Abbot controversy, MIT's faculty voted by a roughly 2-to-1 margin to adopt a formal university statement on freedom of expression.<ref name=Bray2023>{{cite newspaper |last=Bray |first=Hiawatha |title=After Dorian Abbot firestorm, MIT faculty vows to respect ‘free expression’ |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/01/06/metro/after-dorian-abbot-firestorm-mit-faculty-vows-respect-free-expression/ |date=6 January 2023 |newspaper=Boston Globe |access-date=10 October 2025}}</ref><ref name="MFSA 2022">{{cite web | url=https://mitfreespeech.org/docs/2022.12.27_FEWG+Statement+Adoption+Press+Release.pdf | type=Press release | title=MIT Faculty Vote to Accept New Free Expression Statement Supported by MIT Free Speech Alliance | author=<!--Not stated--> | editor=Peter Bonilla and Eric Rasmusen | website=MIT Free Speech Alliance | access-date=May 6, 2023 | url-status=live | archive-url=https://archive.today/https://www.mitfreespeech.org/mit-faculty-vote-to-accept-new-free-expression-statement | archive-date=6 May 2023}}</ref> Abbot said of the faculty statement: "The challenge is always enforcement, but it looks promising."<ref name=Bray2023/>
